Madam President, members of the Security Council, thank you for convening this important meeting. On the situation in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, comes at a critical moment. While the fragile ceasefire in Gaza and regional tensions can consume much of the international community's attention, the West Bank is at the breaking point. And this has not been a sudden deterioration. It's the result of the decades of unresolved conflict that has deepened the unlawful Israeli occupation. driven the Palestinian Authority to the brink of collapse and undermined the prospects for an independent, viable and sovereign Palestinian state. In my briefing to this Council last month, I described the explosive dynamics unfolding in the West Bank. Today, I would like to highlight several developments that are deepening instability while moving us farther away from negotiated end to the conflict. I will begin with the sobering human toll. As of 10th of August, 76 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank in 2026, including 18 children by Israeli forces or settlers. In 2026, three Israelis, including one civilian and two members of the Israeli security forces, were killed in confrontations with Palestinians and in an alleged ramming by a Palestinian in the West Bank. 127 Palestinian communities have experienced full or partial displacement, since January 2023, including 47 that have been entirely displaced, affecting more than 6,390 Palestinians. In 2026 alone, about 3,800 Palestinians, nearly half of them children, have been displaced due to settler violence, demolitions and evictions. Settler violence has reached unprecedented levels. So far this year, the UN has documented more than 1,430 incidents involving Israeli settlers that resulted in casualties, property damage, or both, affecting approximately 260 Palestinian communities, and many incidents occurred in the presence of Israeli forces. Nablus governorate has been particularly hard hit by recent violence. On 24th of July, Israeli settlers attacked Tel village, triggering an escalation which left four Palestinians and two members of Israeli security forces killed. Hundreds of settlers then carried out multiple attacks resulting in Palestinian injuries and extensive property damage. That same day, large groups of settlers attacked the village of Ureef and Sara, also in southwest of Nablus, causing injuries and extensive damage to Palestinian property. Similar incidents are occurring on daily basis across the West Bank. While accountability for such crimes remains rare, I note the 6 August indictment of an Israeli settler in connection with the July 2025 killing of Palestinian community activist Adwa Atalin in the South Hebron Hills. Last year, I visited Adwa's family as they were mourning his death and I experienced firsthand the grief of this entire community. All perpetrators of such crimes must be brought to justice. Madam President, the pattern is clear. Palestinian populations are increasingly being forcibly displaced from villages across the West Bank before the settlers seize the vacated land. Settler attacks, which were previously concentrated in areas C, are increasingly reported in area A and even in area B and even in area A. Israeli military operations and movement restrictions continue to disrupt civilian life and humanitarian operations while refugee camps particularly affected. From 5 to 7 August, Israeli forces conducted a large operation in Qalandia refugee camp, resulting in dozens of Palestinians injured, more than 60 people arrested or detained, and extensive property damage. On 27 July, Israeli forces and officials again entered the UNRWA Qalandia training center without authorization while classes were in session. I reiterate that UN premises are inviolable and immune from any form of interference. Tensions also have increased in East Jerusalem. On 23 July, during Tisha B'Av, large organized Israeli visits to Haram al-Sharif, including by an Israeli minister, again raised concerns over the preservation of the status quo at the holy sites. Madam President, alongside the mounting violence, Israel has significantly accelerated settlement activities while consolidating its control across the occupied West Bank. Since the beginning of this year, Israeli planning authorities advanced or approved approximately 1,360 housing units in the occupied West Bank, including 7,200 housing units in Area C and 5,160 housing units in East Jerusalem. Significant resources are being allocated towards settlement expansion. On 14 July, the government announced some $431 million of US dollars to support the establishment of 34 new settlements approved earlier this year. The funding will finance infrastructure and prefabricated housing. Israeli authorities described this decision as strengthening Israel's hold on the West Bank and preventing the establishment of a Palestinian state. On the administrative task implementation of reforms transferring planning, land management and heritage responsibilities in the West Bank from the military administration to Israeli civilian authorities continued further entrenching Israeli civilian governments. The IDF also issued an unprecedented seizure order for privately owned land in Area A near Kabatya, south of Jenin City to construct a road linking Noa and the main Dotan two of the 34 settlements recently approved. This marks the first seizure of Area A land explicitly for settlement infrastructure. These developments are taking place as the PA, Palestinian Authority fiscal crisis remains acute. According to the PA, Israel is withholding some of $6 billion in clearance revenues preventing the PA from paying full salaries and delivering basic services. Meanwhile, Palestinian financial stability faces a looming threat from the 1st September when Israeli correspondent banks plan to end arrangements for processing shekel transactions. The extension of the indemnity waiver for the year end is welcome but insufficient. Sustained engagement between regulators is needed to secure a durable arrangement. The Palestinian authorities reform efforts also must continue as outlined in Security Resolution 2803. Furthermore, I welcome ongoing preparations ahead of the planned 28 November Palestinian legislative elections, including steps to update voter registration and publish the electoral.

Timetable.

All stakeholders must facilitate credible, inclusive and transparent arrangements enabling all eligible Palestinians to exercise their electoral rights across the occupied Palestinian territory. Madam President, the situation in West Bank must be treated as an emergency requiring urgent action. The concern is not only the continued expansion of the settlements, but the speed and systematic manner in which new facts are being created on the ground. New outposts are established often with state support and can be retroactively authorized or incorporated into a wider settlement system. From these outposts, settler violence and intimidation have driven the displacement of Palestinian community. The spread of agricultural and grazing outposts is deeply troubling as well. Requiring only a small number of settlers, they enable control over vast areas of land. Israeli monitoring organization reported agricultural and pastoral outposts now exercise effective control over close to 20% of the West Bank. On 10 August, members of my team participated in a PA-led diplomatic visit to Bethlehem Governorate, where only some 7% of the land falls under Area A. They observed firsthand the impact of Israeli policies constricting Palestinian movement while enabling encroachment, including incursions at the historic site of Solomon's Falls in Area A. Madam President, we must be clear-eyed about what's taking place. These are interconnected steps, not isolated developments. They are reshaping the West Bank, weakening Palestinian governance, and advancing the fact annexation. The stakes are high. If the West Bank continues to unravel, it will not only undermine the implementation of the Security Council resolution 2803, which is the immediate focus of international community, but it will further erode the prospects for ending occupation and realizing a negotiated Israeli-Palestinian peace based on the two-state solution. We have the means to prevent further deterioration and advance a credible path forward. There is a broad consensus on the essential element of such path, Security Council resolution 2803 must be implemented immediately and in full. The New York Declaration must be implemented together with the resolution 2803 in a complementary and mutually reinforcing manner. Together and within the framework of the existing Council resolution, including resolution 2334, they can provide the political vision and coordinated international effort needed to end the local occupation, advance the two-state solution, and resolve the conflict. We must act now collectively and determinedly to ensure concrete steps are taken towards that objective. Yemen remains committed to support all efforts in support of lasting peace between the Israelis and Palestinians based on 1967 borders with Jerusalem as the capital of both states and both nations living in peace side by side. Thank you very much for your attention, Madam President.

Madam President, Excellencies, thank you to Denmark for convening this important briefing. We meet as the situation facing children across the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, continues to deteriorate. A grandmother told UNICEF colleagues that she was afraid to even step out of her home to put the rubbish outside because of nearly daily settler attacks. She described how an improvised incendiary grenade was thrown into her kitchen, setting the house on fire while her grandchildren were inside. She has since covered the windows with corrugated iron to try to protect her family. But the persistent sense of fear and insecurity haunts them, particularly for the safety of children while traveling to and from school. Imagine raising children under conditions like this. Living behind metal covered windows, afraid to step outside, afraid of what might happen to your children on the way to school, afraid of being exposed to violence in your home. For far too many Palestinian families, these fears have become part of daily life. Over the past three years, settler violence and increasingly militarized operations have escalated sharply across the West Bank. Children have been killed and injured, families have been displaced, homes, schools and essential infrastructure have been attacked or destroyed. And the fundamental spaces of childhood, the home, the classroom, the street, the community, are becoming increasingly unsafe. Excellencies, the numbers tell us just how grave the situation has become. Between January 2024 and the end of July this year, 174 Palestinian children were verified killed by the UN in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. That is more than one child every week. More than 1,500 were injured. Nearly half of those injured were wounded by live ammunition. Over the same period, three Israeli children were killed and 15 injured. Boys, particularly adolescent boys, account for most of the children who have been killed and injured. The UN continues to monitor and verify grave violations against children in the West Bank. These include incidents in which children were shot when they did not pose an imminent threat. Some were shot while running away, while others were simply caught in the violence around them. At the same time, incidents of settler violence are increasing. These have resulted in grave violations against children, which have been identified by the Secretary-General in his latest annual report on children in armed conflict. These incidents leave more than physical wounds. Children who survive serious injuries may live with disabilities for the rest of their lives. Some face arrest. Others struggle to return to school. Exposing a child to violence, raids, intimidation, and displacement takes a profound psychological toll. Parents tell us about children struggling to sleep, children who are afraid to leave home, children withdrawing from school and their communities. And parents tell us something equally devastating, that they no longer feel capable of keeping their children safe. That is a terrible reality for any parent, and it is a terrible reality for any child. Excellencies, the impact extends far beyond those children directly affected by the violence. According to the education cluster, more than 800,000 children in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, face barriers to safe and continuous education because of school closures, insecurity, movement restrictions, and damage to infrastructure. In 2026 alone, 99 education-related incidents were documented, including children being killed, injured, or detained in or on their way to schools, schools being demolished, school buildings being used by military forces, and children being denied access to education. Parents are struggling to keep their children learning when the journey to school itself can be dangerous. According to OCHA, across the West Bank, more than 900 additional movement barriers and restrictions have been imposed over the past two and a half years. Many gates are frequently closed, which results in highly restricted access to movement and essential services, including access to health services and water sources. In a recent UNICEF mission to the West Bank, colleagues were told that settler attacks have damaged water infrastructure and equipment, including water network and storage tanks. This has resulted in reduced access to safe water and other basic water and sanitation and hygiene services. In some areas, developing new water sources is impeded and as a result, residents now are forced to rely on expensive water trucking. Access restrictions are further compounded by repeated intimidation at checkpoints that deter or delay civilians from attempting a crossing. Excellencies, the situation of children in detention is also deeply concerning. According to the Israel Prison Service, at least 355 Palestinian children from the West Bank are currently held in Israeli military detention, the highest number in eight years. Nearly half, 164 children, are held under administrative detention without charge or trial. Children in detention continue to report violence, ill-treatment, humiliating and degrading treatment, and harsh conditions. with a pattern of inadequate nutrition and hygiene for children, resulting in extreme weight loss and rampant scabies infection amongst child detainees. This year, a UNICEF partner spoke to a boy who was arrested from his home in the middle of the night, faced physical violence, was hand-tied, blindfolded, and faced various violations. While being interrogated, the child was held in solitary confinement for over 20 days. Excellencies, the dire situation for children is being compounded by growing obstacles to humanitarian access and essential services. Local authorities have had tax revenues withheld and are unable to pay health and education workers, affecting children's access to basic services. Children requiring medical treatment must be able to reach it. Humanitarian workers and partners must be able to reach children safely wherever those children live. Despite those challenges, UNICEF and our partners remain on the ground. When families are forcibly displaced, UNICEF and partners provide emergency assistance, mental health and psychosocial services, cash, drinking water and hygiene, and support to continue their education. But humanitarian assistance can only mitigate the consequences. It cannot remove the causes. That requires political action. So today, I leave this Council with four urgent requests. First, protect children. Protect children. International humanitarian law and international human rights law must be strictly observed and followed. Law enforcement standards must be respected, with lethal force used only when strictly unavoidable to protect life. Specific safeguards must be put in place wherever children may be present. The administrative detention of children must end, and all practices concerning Palestinian children in the military justice system must be brought into line with international juvenile justice and child rights standards. We echo the call of the Secretary-General in urging Israel to agree and implement an action plan with the United Nations to end and prevent grave violations against children. Second, end the forced displacement of Palestinian children and families. Member states must use their political and diplomatic influence to prevent further displacement and signal zero tolerance for violence against children, families, and communities. Third, protect children's access to education, health care, and other essential services. Children must be able to reach school safely, and children requiring medical treatment must be able to reach hospitals and health facilities. Lastly, protect humanitarian operations. Vital supplies must be allowed into and across the West Bank without unnecessary delay. Public services upon which children and families depend must be protected from interruption. And humanitarian organizations and their partners must be able to operate safely, independently, and without administrative measures that prevent them from reaching children in need. Excellencies, the humanitarian consequences of what is happening in the West Bank are profound. But behind every statistic is a child, a child afraid to walk to school, a child recovering from a gunshot wound, a child held in detention, a child watching her family home being demolished, and a child sleeping behind corrugated iron because her grandmother is trying to keep fire from coming through the window again. These should not be the defining experiences of childhood. Children in the West Bank have the same rights as children everywhere, to live, to learn, to be protected, and to imagine a future beyond violence and fear. UNICEF will continue to advocate for the protection of all children and to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to every child we can reach. But humanitarian organizations cannot create the political conditions that children need to be safe. That responsibility rests with member states who have the power to change them. Thank you, Madam President.

Special attention ought to be paid to protecting humanitarian workers, as well as the continuity of essential services, especially in the areas of healthcare, education, water, and sanitation. Madam President, the government of my country is convinced that the response to the current challenges must be part of a broader political perspective. The international community ought to continue to support efforts to create conditions for a lasting peace that is based upon dialogue, respect for international law, and due regard for legitimate concerns, security concerns of all parties. The DRC also recognizes legitimate concerns with regard to security of Israel and underscores that these, as well as protection of civilians, ought to be taken into account while fully respecting international law. We therefore encourage all parties to exercise restraint, pursue dialogue, and abstain from any actions that could exacerbate the situation on the ground. Only a credible negotiated political process that is based upon the relevant UN resolutions will bring about a just, comprehensive, and lasting peace that provides populations the security, dignity, and stability that they legitimately aspire to. Madam President, in closing, the DRC reaffirms its commitment to upholding international law, to protecting civilian populations, and to seeking a lasting political solution.

We remain convinced that the path of dialogue.

Restraint, and cooperation ought to prevail over that of confrontation in order to maintain prospects for peace and stability in the region. The DRC thus calls upon the international community to continue its efforts steadily and with determination in order to pave the way.

For a lasting peace based upon coexistence, dignity, and security for all. Thank you.
I thank the representative of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and I give the floor to the representative of Liberia.

Thank you. Thank you, Madam President. Liberia thanks the Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process and the Deputy Executive Director of UNICEF for their qualified briefings. One was born and Liberia was among the first to recognize it. The other has spent nearly eight decades caught in the cruel physics of occupation, displacement, and unfulfilled promise. Over 33,000 Palestinians remain forcibly displaced from Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nour Shams, their homes emptied, their right of return denied. acceleration of the E1 settlement project and ongoing land grabs threaten to sever the West Bank in two dealing an irreversible blow to any viable contiguous Palestinian future these are not administrative adjustments they are the systematic burial of peace yet Liberia's clarity remains absolute on two non-negotiable principles. First, security is indivisible. No durable peace can ever take root while Israelis live while Israelis live under the terror of attacks. We condemn such violence unequivocally. Concurrently, we condemn with equal severity the unbearable suffering inflicted upon Palestinian civilians, where women and children bear the catastrophic brunt of a crisis not of their making. Hamas, an armed faction that holds a population's statehood hostage to its own survival, paradoxically undermines the very liberation and much needed statehood it claims to pursue. The full implementation of resolution 2803 and the decommissioning of non-state weapons are essential to establishing one legitimate government, one law, and one accountable security authority. The Secretary General's reports record a staggering scale of violence and violations against children across the region. Protection, return, accountability, and viability. If we fail these four tests, let us then drop the diplomatic pretense. We are not preserving a two-state solution. We are presiding over its slow motion disappearance. History will not ask whether this council issued enough press statements or debated the Middle East and Palestinian question time without number. It will ask whether when the window for peace was being sealed shut beneath concrete and violence, we had the courage to act. Excellencies, Liberia cast its vote for two states in 1947. 79 years later, we continue to stand for the security of both peoples. the dignity of both peoples, and the absolute right of their children to inherit a future defined by peace, definitely not by perpetual war. I thank you for your kind attention.
I thank the representative of Liberia for the statement, and I now give the floor to the representative of Pakistan.

Thank you, Madam President. The distinguished permanent representative of Liberia just reminded, and very rightly, this council of its responsibilities towards the situation that we are discussing. And the two briefings we have heard today are, in fact, calls for action. The situation as presented is grave. The figures quoted speak for themselves. These are interconnected steps building on decades of conflict and occupation. that are undermining the prospects of the two-state solution. Fourth, Israel must respect the historical and legal status quo at the holy sites, including Al-Aqsa Mosque. Al-Haram Al-Sharif and halt all provocative actions. Fifth, Security Council Resolution 2803 and the comprehensive peace plan must be implemented fully and in good faith. The council must have a serious discussion how to tackle the obstacles and violations. When President, as the foreign ministers of the group of eight Arab and Islamic countries, including Pakistan, affirmed on 6th August in their statement, the ongoing Israeli violations in the Gaza Strip cannot be viewed in isolation from the attacks carried out by settlers in the occupied West Bank, the unlawful expansion of settlements, and the unilateral measures aimed at altering the status quo in occupied Jerusalem. Taken together, these practices constitute a systematic policy aimed at imposing a fait accompli by force, undermining the foundations of the two-state solution. Madam President, the situation is approaching a dangerous tipping point. Unless this trajectory is reversed, the consequences for the two state solution and for peace and stability across the region could be catastrophic. The path to peace is clear. It lies in ending the Israeli occupation and enabling the Palestinian people to exercise their inalienable right to self-determination through the establishment of an independent, sovereign, viable, and contiguous state of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. It is the only credible foundation for a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace in the region. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Pakistan for the statement. And I now give the floor to the representative of the Russian Federation.

Madam President, Russia supported the convening of today's Security Council meeting with a goal, with a focus on situation in the West Bank. We believe it's unacceptable to further erode international attention toward the task of achieving a just and lasting Middle East settlement, the cornerstone of which.

Was and remains the Palestinian-Israeli conflict. The confrontation, which decades later remains the key irritant in the region, perpetuating its general state of crisis.

And causing new flashpoints of tension to emerge in the broader Middle East region. We thank the Deputy Special Coordinator of the UN for the Middle East Peace Process, Ramez Al-Khobar, and the Deputy Executive Director of UNICEF, Hanan Suleiman for their detailed briefings on the situation in the West Bank. We agree with the alarming assessments of these UN representatives.

Essentially, the West Bank is approaching a point of no return with a risk of profound destabilization of the political situation in the entire region. The reasons for this dangerous trend are well known. They lie in the creeping expansion of Israel, in the OPT, the escalation of settlement activity, of settlement violence, and the unprecedented tightening of Israeli restrictions on the movement of Palestinian residents. Against the position of most of the international community, West Jerusalem continues its illegal policy of building new settlements. A few days ago, the government issued yet another tender for the construction of over 600 housing units in the province of Ramallah Al-Bireh. Settler violence has reached extreme levels, and it's carried out not only with impunity, but sometimes with the connivance of Israeli soldiers. In late July, early August, there was a wave of attacks carried out in a number of cities in which radicals burned mosques, ravaged homes and vehicles, and dozens of people were injured. According to openly available sources, the settler violence is reaching tragic new levels. Since the beginning of this year, over 11,000 attacks have been committed. Israeli civilians have killed over 20 West Bank civilians. In parallel, we're seeing intensifying IDF operations. to clear West Bank towns and refugee camps. These armed raids are accompanied by arbitrary arrests of Palestinians and large-scale restrictions on their movement. Especially troubling is the fact that due to these measures, the largest Palestinian towns are blockaded, and even emergency medical services have been suspended. We call on Israel to refrain from any arbitrary measures, including settlement activity, that undermine the prospects for a two-state solution, as well as to take effective measures to curb settler violence and to immediately return to implementing relevant UNSC and GA resolutions. Madam President, Of equal concern is the volatile situation in another part of the OPT, that is Gaza. The practical implementation of the American peace plan for Gaza has essentially stalled. Certainly it's important to note that thanks to the efforts of mediators, large-scale bloodshed has ceased in the enclave. However, the ceasefire regime continues to be systematically violated, mainly by Israel. This is clearly demonstrated by the numbers of victims. In less than a year since the formal entry into effect of the ceasefire, Israelis have killed almost 1,300 Palestinians. Among them, according to UNICEF figures, there are almost 300 children. That means that over the past 300 days in Gaza, on average, one child has been killed per day by Israeli soldiers. Despite this tragic reality, here at the Security Council, a number of Western delegations have over the past few months placed the entire responsibility for the stagnation of the Gaza peace plan on Hamas alone. We all recall how during Security Council meetings, the leadership of Hamas were insistently called upon to immediately lay down their arms, not to hinder the work of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, and to accept the roadmap of the High Representative of the Board of Peace, Nikolai Moldanov. We'd like to hope that our Western colleagues will show the same unity and resolve with regard to the other party to the conflict in light of the public rejection of the roadmap by West Jerusalem while Hamas has agreed to the deal. Madam President, we've repeatedly noted that success of any peace initiative on Middle East settlement will be measured by the achievement of its chief goal, the creation of a single, independent, and contiguous state of Palestine and the West Bank and Gaza with its capital in East Jerusalem. the creation of a state coexisting in peace and security with Israel. As demonstrated by the experience of the past few years, it's impossible to resolve the Palestinian issue as well as the entire spectrum of Middle East settlement issues hastily or through the promotion of ad hoc backroom schemes. Equally futile are attempts of certain countries to monopolize the role of mediator. especially when the principal mediator acts solely in the interests of one side of the Arab-Israeli conflict. Under these circumstances, one can hardly expect to see justice or the fulfillment of the aspirations of the Palestinian people. However, an alternative path remains open, achieving lasting stability and an improved situation in the Middle East is possible and necessary through coordinated international and regional efforts that rely on the extensive international legal basis for settlement, the cornerstone of which is the two states for two peoples formula.

Thank you.
I thank the representative of the Russian Federation for the statement. And I now give the floor to the representative of Panama.

Thank you, Madam President. Panama is grateful for the convening of this meeting. We thank Mr. Ramiz Alakbarov, Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, and Ms. Hanan Suleiman, Deputy Executive Director of UNICEF, for their invaluable and moving testimony. Moreover, we recognize the presence of the representatives of the state of Israel and the observer state of Palestine. They are with us in the chamber this morning. We note with grave concern the increasing worsening of the situation in the West Bank that has been described by the briefers with figures. The recent escalation of violence and intimidation continues to claim lives, trigger the displacement of communities, and worsen the humanitarian situation. In addition, we're seeing restrictions placed on movement that continue to stymie access to the civilian population and their access to crucial services, including emergency medical care and livelihoods. That, in turn, worsens the conditions endured by the most vulnerable communities. With dramatic lucidity, Ms. Hannah Solomon described just that in her briefing. She said that those that most acutely suffer the consequences of this situation include children. The continuation of violence, the rising tide of attacks and forced displacement do not only affect the West Bank that is the subject of this meeting. These phenomena also undermine the development, well-being and access of many children to safe, uninterrupted education. As such, we reiterate the importance of guaranteeing safe, continued access without fear or intimidation. And indeed, this access to education must also be uninterrupted. Protecting children and access to education, as well as ensuring the availability of adequate medical treatment, are all crucial components of preserving community resilience and of laying the basis for a lasting peace. Schools must remain safe spaces for learning and protection. They must be free of fear, intimidation and spared the effects of the conflict. Any impact on educational infrastructure or any disruption to educational access undermines children's prospects for their future. President Violence does not only claim lives and destroy livelihoods, it also fuels a climate of ongoing relentless fear that limits freedom of movement, that exposes victims of attacks to displacement risks, and this violence also undermines their physical and mental health because daily activities such as leaving houses become a constant source of concern and insecurity. Consequently, protecting civilians must continue to remain an immediate priority. This must be done with stringent adherence to international law, including international humanitarian law and the relevant resolutions of this Council. Against this backdrop, Panama reiterates its support for the work that the United Nations and its agencies continue to do. We particularly commend the laudable work of UNICEF done alongside international humanitarian organizations and local ones to afford assistance to civilians. We commend their work to protect children, to support efforts aimed at preserving stability too. This work must be able to continue safely in an independent and impartial fashion, while international law is stringently upheld, including international humanitarian law. We call for humanitarian personnel to be protected and full, safe, unfettered, continued humanitarian access for those who require it must be provided. The continuation of violence, the lack of political progress, continued attacks and measures which fan the flames of tension continue to undermine the conditions necessary for the preservation of a credible peace. Any unilateral action which alters the reality on the ground is incompatible with the spirit and goals of this Council's relevant resolutions, including resolution 2334 of 2016. The implementation thereof remains vital if we are to preserve the foundations for a just lasting and mutually acceptable peace. As such, it is vital that we see the resumption of a credible political process. We must bolster confidence and trust, champion a reformed Palestinian Authority able to discharge effectively its responsibilities, and we must avoid unilateral acts which continue to further dim the prospects for a negotiated solution in accordance with international law and the relevant resolutions of the United Nations. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Panama for the statement and I now give the floor to the representative of China.

Thank you, President. First of all, China extends its deepest condolences to the victims of the massive earthquake in Colombia and expresses its sincere sympathies to the bereaved family and the injured. We are confident that under the leadership of their government, the Colombian people will surely join forces to overcome this disaster as soon as possible and rebuild their homes. China supports the convening of this emergency meeting of the Security Council, which is both timely and necessary. I thank Special Deputy Special Coordinator Alaa Bakr and Deputy Executive Director Suleiman for their briefings. For some time now, the situation in the West Bank and Gaza has seen a sharp deterioration, leading to more pain and suffering to the Palestinian people. At its core, this is due to the fact that the fundamental principles of the international law have not been respected, while the Palestinian people's rights to survival and development long ignored, the lives of the Palestinian peoples are just as precious as those of any other people. The international community must uphold a clear sense of right and wrong, further build consensus, promptly correct all erroneous words and deeds that deny or infringe upon the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people and ensure their equal rights so as to effectively uphold international fairness and justice. Second, decisive and effective action must be taken to stop conflict and violence. The situation in the West Bank has been escalating dangerously. The occupying power is pushing forward with settlement expansions, desecrating and vandalizing religious sites, blockading refugee camps and carrying out mass arrests, while settler violence is intensifying. It is shocking that the training center of UNRWA has been forcibly stormed on two occasions. The protection of civilians is not an empty catchword, but an obligation under international law that the occupying power must fulfill. Israel must implement Security Council Resolution 2334, seize settlement activities, curb settler violence, and ensure strict accountability. The agency's normal functioning in accordance with its mandate must be respected. The situation in Gaza is equally concerning. Even after the announcement by the Board of Peace of progress on the second phase of the ceasefire, Israel has continued to refuse to halt its operations. It has now been more than 300 days since the signing of the peace agreement of the ceasefire agreement, yet a lasting ceasefire has yet to be achieved. The current situation is not due to a lack of ceasefire proposal, but a lack of a political will to implement one. China calls on Israel and all relevant parties to implement fully and in good faith the Gaza ceasefire agreement and urges Israel to comply with international humanitarian law by lifting restrictions on the entry of humanitarian supplies countries that have significant over the parties should take concrete actions to de-escalate the situation. Third, we must stay the course and make every effort to revitalise the political prospects of the two-state solution. The two-state solution is the only viable path to resolving the Palestinian issue, as recognised by the international community. Any hesitation, scepticism or wavering is unacceptable. Both Gaza and the West Bank are integral parts of the State of Palestine. Israel must end its illegal occupation of the Palestinian territories as soon as possible and cease undermining the governance structures of the Palestinian National Authority. The international community should fully respect the will of the Palestinian people, advance post-war reconstruction in Gaza in accordance with the principle of Palestinians governing Palestine, return to the correct path of the two-state solution and realize the early establishment of an independent Palestinian state. Only in this way can peace full coexistence between Palestine and Israel be achieved and lasting peace and stability in the Middle East be secured. Madam President, on the question of Palestine, China has always been on the side of peace, justice and conscience. China will, as always, support the just cause of the Palestinian people to realize their legitimate national rights, work to bring an early end to the suffering of the Palestinian people and make unremitting efforts to restore stability to the region and bring peace to its people. Thank you, Madam President.
I thank the representative of China for the statement and I now give the floor to the representative of Bahrain.

Mr. President, we commend the convening of this timely meeting at such a sensitive time we thank the briefers Mr. Ramz alakbarov uh Deputy special coordinator and Madam Suliman executive Deputy executive director of UNICEF for their briefings we stress the following the Kingdom of Bahrain has has supported International and Regional efforts to end the conflict in the Gaza Strip including the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict and the role undertaken by the Board of Peace to support practical measures to strengthen stability, reconstruction, improve the living conditions and pave the way for a credible and serious peace process. This has stoked the suffering of civilians, including that of children, and undermined efforts for calm and peace. We are concerned by the escalation of violence against the Palestinian people in the West Bank. This rise has been unprecedented. 76 Palestinian civilians have been killed since early 2026, according to the United Nations. In conclusion, the Kingdom of Bahrain stresses that East Jerusalem is an integral part of Palestine, which encompasses the West Bank and Gaza. It is the capital of the State of Palestine that must be established along the 4th of June 1967 borders. a state that lives side by side in peace and security with Israel to pave the way for the two-state solution and ensure regional integration to foster stability, security and prosperity for all peoples of the region. I thank you.
Thank you, representative of Bahrain for the statement. And I now give the floor to the representative of Somalia.

Madam President, allow me to begin by thanking Deputy Special Coordinator Alakbarov and UNICEF Deputy Executive Director Suleiman for their updates and for the UN's continued work in the occupied Palestinian territory. Somalia remains deeply troubled by the recent surge in violence across the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem. The past weeks have seen more civilian deaths, injuries, displacement and destruction, worsening an already dire humanitarian and security situation. We unequivocally condemn the growing violence and terrorism from Israeli settlers against Palestinian communities, often in a context where Palestinians are left unprotected. These attacks on civilians are not isolated incidents. They are happening in a wider context of longstanding occupation, illegal settlement expansion, demolitions, evictions, military operations, movement restrictions, land seizures, and ongoing settler violence. Together, these factors are eroding the foundation of Palestinian life in the West Bank. Since January 2025, over 33,000 Palestinians have been forcibly displaced by Israeli military operations in Jenin, Tulkarm, Nur Shams camps, which is the largest displacement since 1967. Many more lives remain at imminent risk. Settler violence is a major driver of this crisis, with more than 1,800 attacks in 2025 alone, affecting some 280 Palestinian communities. This pattern must be reversed. Somalia reiterated that Israeli settlements, including those in East Jerusalem, are a flagrant violation of international law and Security Council Resolution 2334. A worrying development has also been seen in the increasing use of archaeology and heritage claims to justify settlement expansions and restrict Palestinian access to land and holy sites. All actions that alter the status or demographics of the occupied Palestinian territory must stop and reverse immediately. We are particularly alarmed by measures that fragment the Palestinian territory threatening its viability as a contiguous sovereign state. Continued settlement expansion undermines not just future negotiations, but the very basis of the two-state solution. Madam President, as we have heard, the situation for children demands urgent attention. Palestinian children are facing violence, displacement, detention, abuse, and disruption of their education. Prolonged insecurity is inflicting severe psychological distress. School closures, movement restrictions and attacks on education have become unalarmingly common. The ongoing financial crisis and the disruptions to under schools make matters worse. Children must not grow up seeing violence, occupation and displacement as a normal daily occurrence. Their protection and that of schools, hospitals and civilian infrastructure must be guaranteed under international law. The impact, dear colleagues, goes beyond children. Restrictions on movement and access are affecting health care, livelihoods, water and sanitation. and are making it harder for humanitarian organizations to provide assistance. Humanitarian workers themselves face growing danger and obstacles. We are especially concerned by the recent incursions into UNRWA premises in East Jerusalem, including repeated unauthorized entries by Israeli security forces. Such incidents cannot be normalized. UN premises must be respected and protected, and UNRWA's vital work must not be jeopardized. Somalia is also concerned about the deteriorating situation facing the Palestinian Authority, especially with the occupying power's withholding of hundreds of millions of collected tax revenues, which undermine the provision of basic services. Weakening Palestinian institutions while settlement expansion accelerates moves us further from peace. Accountability is essential. Violence by settlers must not go unpunished. Restraint and de-escalation must be prioritized. Yet restraint alone will not solve the root causes, which are entrenched in occupation, settlement expansion, and the lack of credible political horizon. The West Bank and Gaza are one territory and must be governed by a single legitimate Palestinian authority. A political process that ignores this will not bring lasting peace. Somalia stands firmly for the inalienable right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and to an independent and sovereign state of Palestine based on the 1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. The council must ensure that just and lasting solution remains achievable. We call on Israel as the occupying power for an immediate end to settlement activity and violence, full respect for international law, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, especially children, and real accountability for violations, including ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity. Madam President, above all, unless the international community and this council turns commitment to this two-state solution into meaningful action, we are maintaining the status quo of Israeli occupation, perpetual violence and suffering for the Palestinians, including children, and the people of the region. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Somalia for the statement, and I now give the floor to the representative of the United States.

Thank you, Madam President, and thank you to our briefers this morning. As the United States has said many times, we strongly condemn violence by any party in the West Bank. The United States will continue to work constructively to increase security, reduce tensions, and enhance stability that is beneficial for both Israelis and Palestinians alike. President Trump's 20-point plan to end the Gaza conflict makes clear that the PA must verifiably complete a slate of reforms. The United States will not accept compensation for terrorism under the guise of welfare or through any other attempts to evade detection under a different name. The United States reiterates its opposition to annexation of the West Bank. The Security Council must continue to show our strong support to the Port of Peace and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza. They are working to advance President Trump's peace plan, which this Council endorsed in its historic resolution 2803 last November. We also welcome the progress that the Board and the NCAG have achieved so far. This includes boosting humanitarian assistance with safeguards in place to minimize Hamas's stealing and looting of resources. We further welcome the milestone achieved at the end of July when Hamas finally and for the first time committed to an actionable plan for its disarmament. All parties must build on this momentum to full and irreversible disarmament and ensure that Gaza is never again a launching pad for threats to Israel's national security. This path forward, as the Board of Peace has noted, holds the promise of delivering significant benefits to the people of Gaza. Thank you.
I thank the representative of the United States for their statement, and I shall now make a statement in my capacity as the representative of Denmark.

I would like to start by thanking Deputy Special Coordinator Alaa Baraf and Deputy Executive Director Suleiman for their briefings. What we've heard today is not just statistics, as DED Suleiman stressed this morning. It is the daily reality of Palestinian children living under the threat of settler violence, loss of livelihood, demolition and displacement. These realities were also reiterated in the Independent International Commission of Inquiries report examining violations and crimes against Palestinian children that was published in June. At the same time, we hear that July was an exceptionally deadly month in the context of settler related violence. This is why Denmark, together with France, Greece, Latvia and the UK, supported by other Council members, called for this urgent meeting. Colleagues, the two-state solution as chartered in the resolutions of this Council remains the only viable path to resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Last September, 142 states reaffirmed their support for this vision in the New York Declaration. But for this vision to materialize, the current trajectory in the West Bank must urgently be reversed. We would like to emphasize four urgent matters. First, settler violence must stop and those responsible must be held accountable. No Palestinian child should witness homes set ablaze, access to schools hampered, destroyed livelihoods or blocked water sources. We urge the Israeli authorities to take immediate measures to prevent violence, protect civilians and ensure accountability. The European Union has recently put more extremist Israeli settlers and organizations responsible for serious and systematic human rights abuses against Palestinians under sanctions. Second, the expansion of illegal settlements must end immediately. We remain deeply concerned by the potential issuing of tenders for the E1 settlement, which threatens to separate East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank and divide the West Bank in two. We urge businesses to be aware of the potential legal, financial, and reputational risks associated with bidding for these contracts. We once again stress that Security Council Resolution 2334 must be fully implemented. Third, Palestinian children deserve to grow up under a functioning, effective, and reformed Palestinian Authority able to pay salaries and provide essential services. We therefore reiterate our call for Israel to release withheld tax revenues and for the PEA to continue its important work on necessary reforms, including on democracy and good governance. Finally, the developments in the West Bank cannot be separate for what happens in Gaza. The stability of both Gaza and the West Bank is critical to any lasting peace, including to Israel's long-term security. It is in the interest of both Palestinians and Israelis to transition Gaza from war to peace. We took note of the recent news of progress towards an agreement on the disarmament of Hamas and urge all parties to reach a full agreement on this decisive issue. And we continue to call on all parties to fully respect the ceasefire, on Hamas to disarm, and on Israel to ensure the phased withdrawal of the IDF in line with resolution 2803, as well as to ensure unhindered humanitarian aid.
